summary: Gladia's Self-serve plan grants €50 in one-time signup credits valid for one year, not a recurring allowance. The provider estimates roughly 312 hours of Solaria-3 async transcription, 185 hours on Solaria-1, or 73 hours of real-time transcription. Current base rates are €0.16/hour for Solaria-3 async, €0.27/hour for Solaria-1 async, and €0.68/hour for real-time; enabled add-ons such as translation or summarization are billed separately. Includes 30 concurrent real-time sessions and 25 async jobs, speaker diarization and 100+ languages. Self-serve is opted into model training by default, with free opt-out in your profile. Continued usage uses a prepaid wallet with manual or optional automatic top-ups; auto top-up charges your saved payment method and can be disabled in billing settings. The one-year grant validity is not a signup deadline.
claim_steps: Sign up at https://gladia.io on the Self-serve plan.
Use the one-time €50 credit within one year. Approximate alternatives: 312h Solaria-3 async, 185h Solaria-1 async, or 73h real-time; enabled add-ons cost extra.
Check your profile's model-training setting: Self-serve opts in by default, but you can opt out at no extra cost.
After the grant is used, top up the prepaid wallet manually or optionally enable auto top-up. Auto top-up charges your saved payment method; change or disable it in billing settings.

social_proof.title: Gladia pricing FAQ — signup credit and validity
social_proof.text: Yes. New accounts get 50€ in free credits, valid for one year. That's roughly 312 hours of async transcription on solaria-3, 185 hours on solaria-1, or 73 hours of real-time. Once used, top up to continue, or get in touch for a demo.

social_proof.title: Gladia pricing FAQ — model-training opt-out
social_proof.text: Yes, at no extra cost. Self-serve is opted in by default, and you can opt out anytime from your profile. Enterprise is opted out by default.

social_proof.title: Gladia pricing FAQ — prepaid wallet
social_proof.text: Gladia runs on a prepaid credit wallet. You can top up manually, or set auto top-up to refill when your balance drops below a threshold you choose. You'll get notified on low balance, top-ups, and failed payments, so there are no end-of-month surprises.
